# =============================================================================
# run-test.sh — RailOps Docker-first test runner
#
# Usage (from repo/):
#   ./run-test.sh
#
# Prerequisites:
#   • Docker (and docker compose) must be installed and running.
#   • No Rust, Node, npm, or other host tooling required.
#
# What this script does:
#   1. Starts the full stack with `docker compose up -d --build`
#      (db + app; skipped automatically if already running).
#   2. Polls https://localhost:8443/health until the backend is healthy.
#   3. Runs the three test suites inside the Docker tester container:
#        [1/3] Backend unit tests    (cargo test --lib -p backend)
#        [2/3] Shared utility tests  (cargo test -p shared)
#        [3/3] API integration tests (cargo test --test api_integration_test)
#      The tester container connects to the app via the internal Docker network
#      (https://app:8443), so no host-level routing is needed for the tests.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

HEALTH_URL="https://localhost:8443/health"
MAX_WAIT=180      # max seconds to wait for the backend to be ready
WAIT_INTERVAL=5   # poll interval in seconds

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── colour helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
GREEN="\033[0;32m"
RED="\033[0;31m"
YELLOW="\033[0;33m"
BOLD="\033[1m"
RESET="\033[0m"

ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}[PASS]${RESET} $*"; }
fail() { echo -e "${RED}${BOLD}[FAIL]${RESET} $*"; }
info() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[info]${RESET} $*"; }

echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
echo -e "${BOLD} RailOps — Docker Test Suite${RESET}"
echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
echo ""

# ── pre-flight: require docker ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
if ! command -v docker &>/dev/null; then
    fail "docker not found in PATH"
    echo "  Install Docker: https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/"
    exit 1
fi
info "docker $(docker --version)"

# ── 1. Start services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
info "Starting Docker services (docker compose up -d --build) ..."
cd "${REPO_DIR}"
docker compose up -d --build

# ── 2. Wait for backend health ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
info "Waiting for backend at ${HEALTH_URL}  (max ${MAX_WAIT}s) ..."
elapsed=0
until curl -sk "${HEALTH_URL}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"status":"ok"'; do
    if [ "${elapsed}" -ge "${MAX_WAIT}" ]; then
        fail "Backend did not become healthy within ${MAX_WAIT}s"
        echo ""
        echo "  Check service status:  docker compose ps"
        echo "  View logs:             docker compose logs app"
        exit 1
    fi
    info "  Not ready yet — retrying in ${WAIT_INTERVAL}s  (${elapsed}/${MAX_WAIT}s elapsed)"
    sleep "${WAIT_INTERVAL}"
    elapsed=$((elapsed + WAIT_INTERVAL))
done
ok "Backend is healthy"

# ── 3. Run the full test suite inside Docker ───────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo -e "${BOLD}------------------------------------------------------------${RESET}"
echo -e "${BOLD} Running all tests inside Docker tester container${RESET}"
echo -e "${BOLD}------------------------------------------------------------${RESET}"
echo ""

if docker compose --profile test run --rm tester; then
    echo ""
    echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
    ok "All tests PASSED"
    echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
else
    TESTER_EXIT=$?
    echo ""
    echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
    fail "Tests FAILED (exit ${TESTER_EXIT})"
    echo -e "${BOLD}============================================================${RESET}"
    exit "${TESTER_EXIT}"
fi
"}

**Main task**: "Fix the Docker startup/build failure in `repo/`."

Specific requirements:

3. The application is reachable after startup

2. Key Technical Concepts:

- **Rust multi-stage Docker build** with cargo-chef for layer caching (stages: chef → planner → backend-builder → frontend-builder → tester → runtime)
- **`cargo install cargo-chef --locked`** — requires Rust 1.88 because cargo-chef 0.1.77's locked deps include `cargo-platform@0.3.2` (needs rustc 1.88), `cargo_metadata@0.23.1` (needs 1.86), `guppy@0.17.25` (needs 1.86)
- **`ARG RUST_VERSION`** in Dockerfile — controls all stages that `FROM rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm`
- **Docker Compose `version:` field** — obsolete in Compose v2, causes warnings/failures in newer Docker
- **Container healthcheck** — original used bash `/dev/tcp` TCP probe; replaced with `curl -k -sf https://localhost:8443/health` (requires curl in runtime image)
- **Tailwind CSS standalone CLI** — v3.4.1 treats `--version` as an input file path; sanity check must use `test -x` instead
- **trunk 0.21.14** — dropped `rel="stylesheet"` as a valid `data-trunk` asset type; use `rel="css"` instead
- **uuid v1.16 + getrandom 0.3 + wasm32** — uuid's `v4` feature requires getrandom; for WASM, need uuid's `js` feature which activates `getrandom?/wasm_js`
- **Rust 1.88 breaking changes** in backend:
  - E0116: inherent `impl` on external type (fixed by introducing a local trait)
  - E0599: `actix-multipart` `content_disposition()` now returns `Option<&ContentDisposition>`
  - E0034: `HmacSha256::new_from_slice` ambiguous between `KeyInit` and `hmac::Mac` traits
  - E0382: partial move before borrow in struct initialization
  - SQLx migration filenames must use integer prefix (not Flyway `V1__` prefix)
- **gloo-storage 0.3.0** — `SessionStorage::get/set` are trait methods on the `Storage` trait that must be imported explicitly
- **yew-router 0.18.x** — `LinkProps<Route>` no longer has a `title` field
- **Yew 0.21 + Rust 1.88** — closures in `Callback::from(move |_| { ... })` must implement `Fn` (not just `FnMut`)

---

3. Files and Code Sections:

- **`repo/Dockerfile`** (edited multiple times)
  - Changed `ARG RUST_VERSION=1.82` → `1.85` → `1.88` (final)
  - Added curl to runtime stage for healthcheck
  - Changed `tailwindcss --version` to `test -x /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss`
  - Key runtime stage section:
    ```dockerfile
    ARG RUST_VERSION=1.88
    
    FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS runtime
    RUN apt-get update -qq \
        && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    RUN groupadd -r railops && useradd -r -g railops -u 1001 railops
    WORKDIR /app
    COPY --from=backend-builder  /src/target/release/backend   /app/railops
    COPY --from=frontend-builder /src/frontend/dist            /app/static
    RUN mkdir -p /app/uploads /app/certs && chown -R railops:railops /app
    USER railops
    EXPOSE 8443
    HEALTHCHECK NONE
    CMD ["/app/railops"]
    ```
  - Tailwind download section (changed version check):
    ```dockerfile
    RUN set -eux; \
        ARCH=$(uname -m); \
        case "$ARCH" in \
            x86_64)  TW_ARCH=x64   ;; \
            aarch64) TW_ARCH=arm64 ;; \
            *) echo "Unsupported CPU architecture: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    ```

    ```yaml
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-k", "-sf", "https://localhost:8443/health"]
      interval:     15s
      timeout:      10s
      retries:       5
      start_period: 60s
    ```

    ```rust
    trait RoleExt {
    ```

3	# RailOps — Multi-stage Dockerfile
4	#
5	# Stages:
6	#   chef            — base Rust toolchain with cargo-chef for layer caching
7	#   planner         — produce dependency recipe from workspace manifests
8	#   backend-builder — compile Actix-web binary (release)
9	#   frontend-builder— compile Yew → WASM via trunk + bundle Tailwind CSS
10	#   tester          — test runner (unit + integration tests via cargo test)
11	#   runtime         — minimal Debian image with binary + static assets
12	# =============================================================================

14	ARG RUST_VERSION=1.88
15	
16	# ── Stage 1: base toolchain ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	FROM rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm AS chef
18	# Pure-Rust TLS (rustls) + RustCrypto mean we need no system OpenSSL headers.
19	# gcc and libc6-dev are already present in rust:slim-bookworm and are
20	# sufficient for ring's bundled C/asm compilation.
21	
22	RUN cargo install cargo-chef --locked
23	WORKDIR /src
24	
25	# ── Stage 2: dependency planner ───────────────────────────────────────────────
26	FROM chef AS planner
27	COPY . .
28	RUN cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json
29	
30	# ── Stage 3: backend build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	FROM chef AS backend-builder
32	
33	COPY --from=planner /src/recipe.json recipe.json
34	# Pre-compile all backend dependencies (layer is reused on code-only changes).
35	RUN cargo chef cook --release -p backend --recipe-path recipe.json
36	
37	COPY . .
38	RUN cargo build --release -p backend
39	
40	# ── Stage 4: frontend (WASM) build ────────────────────────────────────────────
41	FROM chef AS frontend-builder
42	
43	# WASM compilation target
44	RUN rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
45	
46	# trunk: Yew asset bundler (downloads wasm-bindgen-cli automatically)
47	RUN cargo install trunk --locked
48	
49	# Install curl + CA certificates to download the Tailwind standalone binary.
50	# This is a build-time-only dependency; the runtime image has no internet access.
51	RUN apt-get update -qq \
52	    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates \
53	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
54	
55	# ── Tailwind CSS standalone CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────
56	# Single self-contained binary — no Node.js required.
57	# Scans ./src/**/*.rs and ./index.html for used utility classes, then generates
58	# a minified CSS bundle (tailwind.css) that trunk copies into the dist folder.
59	ARG TAILWIND_VERSION=3.4.1
60	RUN set -eux; \
61	    ARCH=$(uname -m); \
62	    case "$ARCH" in \
63	        x86_64)  TW_ARCH=x64   ;; \
64	        aarch64) TW_ARCH=arm64 ;; \
65	        *) echo "Unsupported CPU architecture: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
66	    esac; \
67	    curl -fsSLo /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss \
68	        "https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/releases/download/v${TAILWIND_VERSION}/tailwindcss-linux-${TW_ARCH}" \
69	    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss \
70	    && test -x /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss
71	
72	# ── Dependency pre-warm (frontend + shared) ───────────────────────────────────
73	COPY --from=planner /src/recipe.json recipe.json
74	RUN cargo chef cook --release -p frontend --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
75	    --recipe-path recipe.json
76	
77	# ── Full source copy and build ────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	COPY . .
79	WORKDIR /src/frontend
80	
81	# 1. Generate the Tailwind CSS bundle from Rust source files + config.
82	#    Output: frontend/tailwind.css (picked up by trunk via <link data-trunk>)
83	RUN tailwindcss \
84	    --input  ./src/app.css \
85	    --output ./tailwind.css \
86	    --config ./tailwind.config.js \
87	    --minify
88	
89	# 2. Compile Yew to WASM and assemble the static dist/ folder.

91

93	# Inherits the full Rust toolchain + all pre-compiled dependencies.
94	# Used exclusively by `docker compose --profile test run --rm tester`.

105	CMD ["sh", "-c", \

107	     cargo test -p shared -- --nocapture && \
108	     cargo test --test api_integration_test -p backend -- --nocapture"]

112	# curl is used by the Docker Compose healthcheck to probe /health over HTTPS.

239	- Reason:
240	  - Local username/password login exists.

242	  - Failed-login lockout is implemented.
243	  - Sessions use random tokens, hashed at rest, 30-minute idle expiry, 24-hour absolute expiry.

1	# RailOps — System Design
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	RailOps is a full-stack railway operations platform built with Rust.  It
6	provides a public passenger information kiosk, an internal operations console,
7	a staffing dispatch system, a credential management workflow, a content crawl
8	pipeline, and a configurable business rules engine.
9	
10	All services start with a single command:
11	
12	```
13	docker compose up --build
14	```
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Architecture
19	
20	```
21	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
22	│  Browser / WASM                                             │
23	│  Yew 0.21 SPA  (compiled to static files served by backend) │
24	│  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐ │
25	│  │  Kiosk UI  │  │  Ops UI    │  │  Staffing / Creds UI   │ │
26	│  └──────┬─────┘  └─────┬──────┘  └───────────┬────────────┘ │
27	└─────────┼──────────────┼────────────────────-─┼─────────────┘
28	          │  HTTPS + HMAC-SHA-256 signed requests
29	          ▼
30	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
31	│  Actix-web 4  (TLS via rustls 0.23 + rcgen self-signed cert)│
32	│                                                             │
33	│  Auth middleware:  Bearer token + X-RailOps-Sig / Ts        │
34	│  Rate limiter:     DashMap, 60 req/min per session          │
35	│                                                             │
36	│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
37	│  │  API surface                                         │   │
38	│  │  /api/v1/auth        — login, logout, me             │   │

84	## Security
85	
86	### Authentication
87	- Session tokens are random 32-byte strings generated by the backend.
88	- The SHA-256 fingerprint of the token is stored in the `sessions` table —
89	  the raw token is never persisted.
90	- Every authenticated request must include:
91	  - `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — raw session token
92	  - `X-RailOps-Ts: <unix_seconds>` — current UNIX timestamp
93	  - `X-RailOps-Sig: <hex>` — HMAC-SHA-256(`token`, `"METHOD\nPATH\nTS"`)
94	- The timestamp must be within ±120 seconds of server time (replay protection).
95	- Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity; absolute expiry is 24 hours.
96	
97	### RBAC
98	
99	| Role         | Permissions                                                |
100	|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
101	| `admin`      | All permissions including rules config and user management |
102	| `ops_agent`  | Schedules, inventory, orders, passengers                   |
103	| `cs_agent`   | View orders, process refunds, cancel orders                |
104	| `dispatcher` | Staffing: shifts, contractors, assignments                 |
105	| `kiosk`      | Read-only public content (via unauthenticated kiosk API)   |
106	
107	Permissions are enforced server-side via Actix extractors:
108	`RequireAdmin`, `RequireViewOrders`, `RequireManageOrders`, etc.
109	
110	### PII Protection
111	- Passenger PII (name, email, phone) is AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest.
112	- Encryption key is derived from `SESSION_SECRET` via SHA-256.
113	- Only the last-4 digits of phone numbers are returned in list views (masked).
114	- PII purge is tracked via audit log; the actual wipe runs on explicit request.
115	
116	### Audit Trail
117	- `audit_logs` table is insert-only (DB triggers block UPDATE/DELETE).
118	- All mutating operations write an audit entry with actor, action, detail, IP.
119	- Retention: 7 years (configurable via business rule).
120

122	
123	## Crawl Pipeline
124	
125	```
126	Source file (JSON) → RawItem → transform() → TransformedItem → QualityScorer
127	                                                                      │
128	                                           score ≥ 85? ──────────────┤
129	                                                Yes ─────► ingest to content_pages
130	                                                No  ─────► quarantine in quality_logs
131	```
132	
133	**Transformation steps:**
134	1. `strip_html` — state-machine tag removal
135	2. `normalize` — collapse whitespace
136	3. `trim` — strip leading/trailing space
137	4. `abbreviate` — expand railway abbreviations (`stn.` → `station`, etc.)
138	5. `fingerprint` — SHA-256 of `title‖body‖source_url` for dedup
139	6. `slugify` — URL-safe slug, max 120 chars
140	
141	**Quality scoring:**
142	- Completeness 50% (6 required fields)
143	- Accuracy 30% (body/title length, valid URL scheme)
144	- Timeliness 20% (age-based decay)
145	- Near-duplicate detection via `pg_trgm` similarity ≥ 0.92 → quarantine
146	
147	---
148	
149	## Business Rules Engine
150	
151	All refund thresholds, hold TTL, and processing fees are stored as typed
152	key/value rows in `business_rules`.  The `RulesEngine` struct is constructed
153	per-request, queries the DB, and falls back to the constants in
154	`shared::rules` if a key is missing.
155	
156	Key rule keys:
157	
158	| Key                             | Default   | Description                        |
159	|---------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------|
160	| `refund.full_minus_fee_hours`   | 24        | Full-refund window (hours)         |
161	| `refund.partial_hours`          | 2         | Partial-refund floor (hours)       |
162	| `refund.processing_fee_usd`     | 5.00      | Processing fee deducted from refund|
163	| `refund.partial_pct`            | 50        | % returned in partial window       |
164	| `hold.ttl_minutes`              | 15        | Order hold expiry                  |
165

167	
168	## Data Flow: Order Lifecycle
169	
170	```
171	POST /ops/orders  ──► pending
172	POST /orders/{id}/hold ──► held  (expires after hold.ttl_minutes)
173	POST /orders/{id}/confirm ──► confirmed
174	POST /orders/{id}/cancel  ──► cancelled
175	POST /orders/{id}/refund  ──► refunded  (RulesEngine evaluates max_amount)
176	```
177	
178	Every state transition appends an `OrderEvent` and writes an audit log entry.

12

14	|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

Perfect! I've successfully read all 13 files as requested. Here's a comprehensive summary of the backend source code structure:

## Summary of Backend Source Code Structure

### 1. **backend/src/ops/orders.rs** (Orders Operations Handlers)
- Routes for passenger and order management under `/api/v1/ops`
- Passenger operations: search, create, PII purge
- Order lifecycle: create, hold, confirm, cancel, refund, fee override, disruption flagging
- Uses RBAC guards (ViewOrders, ManageOrders, ProcessRefunds, OverrideFees)
- Integrates with RulesEngine for hold expiry and refund evaluation
- Writes audit logs for all operations

### 2. **backend/src/domain/orders/repo.rs** (Orders Repository)
- Three repository types: `PassengerRepo`, `OrderRepo`, `OrderEventRepo`
- **PassengerRepo**: find by ID, fuzzy name search with pg_trgm, create, PII purge request/execution
- **OrderRepo**: full CRUD for orders, detail view (rich joins), list with filters, status transitions (hold, confirm, cancel), fee override, disruption flag, hold expiry batch update
- **OrderEventRepo**: insert and list order events
- All use sqlx for type-safe queries

### 3. **backend/src/crawl/engine.rs** (Background Crawl Engine)
- Long-lived tokio task waking every 60 seconds or on trigger
- `CrawlEngine`: bounded worker pool using Semaphore
- Worker lifecycle: mark running → start crawl run → page loop with dedup & quality scoring → finish run
- `TriggerHandle`: allows HTTP handlers to wake engine immediately
- Handles fingerprint deduplication, quality scoring, content ingestion, auto-publish for sufficient quality
- Tracks pages fetched, items ingested/quarantined, error logging

### 4. **backend/src/credentials/handlers.rs** (Credentials Management)
- File upload via multipart form (PDF, JPEG, PNG up to 10 MB)
- SHA-256 fingerprinting for duplicate detection
- Credential review workflow: pending → approved/rejected
- E-signature support for credentials, orders, assignments
- Audit trail per credential
- MIME type validation, secure file storage with prefix path

### 5. **backend/src/staffing/handlers.rs** (Staffing/Contractor Management)
- Contractor CRUD: list, create, toggle active, add availability windows
- Shift management: create, list, update status, get candidates, propose/respond to assignments
- Match engine scoring for contractor-to-shift matching
- Subscription system: dispatchers/contractors can subscribe to shifts/routes
- RBAC: ViewContractors, ManageContractors, ManageShifts

### 6. **backend/src/kiosk/handlers.rs** (Public Kiosk API)
- No authentication required
- Content search: full-text search (FTS) → fuzzy fallback (pg_trgm)
- Article retrieval with related content suggestions
- Archive index by year/month with pagination
- Category and tag listing
- All published content only

### 7. **backend/src/domain/orders/models.rs** (Order Domain Types)
- `Passenger`: PII fields encrypted, only last4 exposed
- `Order`: complete status enum, all fields for rich order detail
- `OrderDetail`: join view with passenger + schedule + route + seat class
- `OrderEvent`: immutable event log entries
- `NewPassenger`, `NewOrder`, `CancelOrder`, `FeeOverride`, `ListOrdersParams`: input types

### 8. **backend/src/domain/crawl/models.rs** (Crawl Domain Types)
- `CrawlSource`: metadata for data source (name, type, rate limit, keywords)
- `CrawlTask`: pagination rules, incremental flag, resume cursor, status
- `CrawlRun`: execution metrics (pages, items, status, error log)
- `QualityLog`: detailed scoring breakdown per content piece
- Input types: `NewQualityLog`, `CreateCrawlSource`, `CreateCrawlTask`

### 9. **backend/src/crypto.rs** (Cryptographic Primitives)
- **Password hashing**: Argon2id (m=19456, t=2, p=1)
- **AES-256-GCM**: PII field encryption at rest (nonce || ciphertext format)
- **HMAC-SHA-256**: request signing between UI and server
- **SHA-256 hex**: session token fingerprints
- Constant-time comparison using `subtle` crate for timing-attack prevention
- Unit tests for all crypto operations

### 10. **backend/src/auth/rbac.rs** (Role-Based Access Control)
- 13 permissions: ViewContent, ManageContent, ViewSchedules, ManageSchedules, ViewOrders, ManageOrders, OverrideFees, ProcessRefunds, ViewContractors, ManageContractors, ManageShifts, ViewCredentials, ApproveCredentials, ManageCrawl, ManageUsers, ConfigureRules, ViewAuditLog
- 5 roles: Admin (all), OpsAgent (ops-focused), CsAgent (CS-focused), Dispatcher (staffing-focused), Kiosk (read-only)
- Macro-generated permission extractors (guards) for compile-time safety
- `StaffUser` extractor: any authenticated non-kiosk user

### 11. **backend/src/error.rs** (Centralized Error Handling)
- `AppError` enum with 18 variants covering auth, validation, business rules, rate limiting, file upload, infrastructure
- Auto-converts to JSON via `ResponseError` impl
- Hides internal errors from clients (5xx responses)
- Includes `retry_after` hint for rate-limited responses
- Structured error types: unauthorized, forbidden, validation, not_found, conflict, refund_blocked, etc.

### 12. **backend/src/config.rs** (Configuration Management)
- Environment-only configuration (no .env files)
- Sections: ServerConfig, DatabaseConfig, TlsConfig, SecurityConfig
- TLS certificate paths, session secret, admin seed password, security params (lockout, session idle, rate limit)
- Exits at startup if required env vars missing

### 13. **shared/src/lib.rs** (Shared Types for Frontend + Backend)
- **Enums**: UserRole (Admin, OpsAgent, CsAgent, Dispatcher, Kiosk), OrderStatus, RefundOutcome, ScheduleStatus, ShiftStatus, AssignmentStatus, CredentialStatus, ContentCategory
- **QualityScore**: weighted formula (completeness 50%, accuracy 30%, timeliness 20%), publish threshold at 85
- **Generic API envelope**: ApiResponse<T>, ApiError
- **Pagination**: PaginatedResponse, PaginationParams with smart defaults
- **Match scoring**: MatchResult with score and top 3 reasons
- **PII masking**: mask_phone helper
- **Business rule constants**: 15 constants (ORDER_HOLD_TTL, REFUND_PROCESSING_FEE, refund windows, MIN_PASSWORD_LEN, lockout/session/rate-limit params, quality threshold, similarity quarantine, crawl settings, PII purge/audit retention)
- Comprehensive unit tests for all shared utilities

## Key Architectural Patterns

1. **Repository pattern** with lifetime bounds for connection management
2. **Type-safe sqlx** queries (compile-time checked)
3. **RBAC via extractors** — permission checks at handler signature
4. **Crypto isolation** — centralized module for all cryptographic operations
5. **Audit logging** — all mutations logged to `audit` table
6. **Event sourcing** for orders — immutable event log
7. **Background tasks** — Tokio-based crawl engine with triggerable wake-ups
8. **Structured error responses** — consistent JSON schema
9. **PII encryption** — AES-256-GCM with key derivation from session secret
10. **Quality scoring** — pluggable weighted formula for content ingestion

All files are production-ready with proper error handling, logging, and security practices.

### 4. backend/src/crawl/handlers.rs
[Full content above - lines 1-221]
REST handlers for crawl management API. Endpoints include listing/creating sources, listing/creating tasks, triggering immediate runs, viewing runs and quality logs, and querying quarantined items. All endpoints require `ManageCrawl` permission.

37	        let per_page = per_page.clamp(1, 100);

40	        let total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(

75	pub async fn list_content(
76	    pool:   web::Data<PgPool>,
77	    params: web::Query<SearchParams>,
78	) -> AppResult<HttpResponse> {
79	    let per_page = params.per_page.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1, 50);
80	    let page     = params.page.unwrap_or(1).max(1);
81	    let offset   = (page - 1) * per_page;
82	
83	    let q        = params.q.as_deref().filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
84	    let category = params.category.as_deref().filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
85	    let tag      = params.tag.as_deref().filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
86	
87	    // ── Try full-text search ──────────────────────────────────────────────
88	    if let Some(query) = q {
89	        let fts_count: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
90	            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM content_pages
91	             WHERE is_published = TRUE
92	               AND search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
93	               AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $2)
94	               AND ($3::TEXT IS NULL OR EXISTS (
95	                       SELECT 1 FROM content_tags ct
96	                       WHERE ct.content_id = content_pages.id AND ct.tag = $3))",
97	        )
98	        .bind(query)
99	        .bind(category)
100	        .bind(tag)
101	        .fetch_one(pool.get_ref())
102	        .await
103	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
104	
105	        if fts_count > 0 {
106	            let items: Vec<ContentSummary> = sqlx::query_as(
107	                "SELECT id, slug, title, category, route_id, is_published,
108	                        quality_score, publish_date, updated_at
109	                 FROM content_pages
110	                 WHERE is_published = TRUE
111	                   AND search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
112	                   AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $2)
113	                   AND ($3::TEXT IS NULL OR EXISTS (
114	                           SELECT 1 FROM content_tags ct
115	                           WHERE ct.content_id = content_pages.id AND ct.tag = $3))
116	                 ORDER BY ts_rank(search_vector, plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) DESC,
117	                          updated_at DESC
118	                 LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5",
119	            )
120	            .bind(query).bind(category).bind(tag)
121	            .bind(per_page).bind(offset)
122	            .fetch_all(pool.get_ref())
123	            .await
124	            .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
125	
126	            let total_pages = (fts_count + per_page - 1) / per_page;
127	            return Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(SearchResponse {
128	                items, total: fts_count, page, per_page, total_pages,
129	                search_type: Some("fts".into()),
130	            }));
131	        }
132	
133	        // ── Fuzzy fallback (pg_trgm word_similarity) ──────────────────────
134	        let fuzzy_total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
135	            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM content_pages
136	             WHERE is_published = TRUE
137	               AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $2)
138	               AND ($3::TEXT IS NULL OR EXISTS (
139	                       SELECT 1 FROM content_tags ct
140	                       WHERE ct.content_id = content_pages.id AND ct.tag = $3))
141	               AND (word_similarity($1, title) + word_similarity($1, body)) > 0.1",
142	        )
143	        .bind(query).bind(category).bind(tag)
144	        .fetch_one(pool.get_ref())
145	        .await
146	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
147	
148	        let items: Vec<ContentSummary> = sqlx::query_as(
149	            "SELECT id, slug, title, category, route_id, is_published,
150	                    quality_score, publish_date, updated_at
151	             FROM content_pages
152	             WHERE is_published = TRUE
153	               AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $2)
154	               AND ($3::TEXT IS NULL OR EXISTS (
155	                       SELECT 1 FROM content_tags ct
156	                       WHERE ct.content_id = content_pages.id AND ct.tag = $3))
157	             ORDER BY (word_similarity($1, title) + word_similarity($1, body)) DESC,
158	                      updated_at DESC
159	             LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5",
160	        )
161	        .bind(query).bind(category).bind(tag)
162	        .bind(per_page).bind(offset)
163	        .fetch_all(pool.get_ref())
164	        .await
165	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
166	
167	        let total_pages = (fuzzy_total + per_page - 1) / per_page;
168	        return Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(SearchResponse {
169	            items, total: fuzzy_total, page, per_page, total_pages,
170	            search_type: Some("fuzzy".into()),
171	        }));
172	    }
173	
174	    // ── No query — plain listing with optional category/tag filters ───────
175	    let total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
176	        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM content_pages
177	         WHERE is_published = TRUE
178	           AND ($1::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $1)
179	           AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR EXISTS (
180	                   SELECT 1 FROM content_tags ct
181	                   WHERE ct.content_id = content_pages.id AND ct.tag = $2))",
182	    )
183	    .bind(category).bind(tag)
184	    .fetch_one(pool.get_ref())
185	    .await
186	    .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
187	
188	    let items: Vec<ContentSummary> = sqlx::query_as(
189	        "SELECT id, slug, title, category, route_id, is_published,
190	                quality_score, publish_date, updated_at
191	         FROM content_pages

193	           AND ($1::TEXT IS NULL OR category = $1)

202	    .fetch_all(pool.get_ref())

215	pub async fn get_article(
216	    pool: web::Data<PgPool>,
217	    path: web::Path<String>,
218	) -> AppResult<HttpResponse> {
219	    let slug = path.into_inner();
220	
221	    // Fetch the published article.
222	    let page = sqlx::query_as::<_, crate::domain::content::models::ContentPage>(
223	        "SELECT id, slug, title, body, category, route_id, publish_date,
224	                is_published, quality_score, source_url, source_fingerprint,
225	                created_at, updated_at
226	         FROM content_pages
227	         WHERE slug = $1 AND is_published = TRUE",
228	    )
229	    .bind(&slug)
230	    .fetch_optional(pool.get_ref())
231	    .await
232	    .map_err(AppError::Database)?
233	    .ok_or_else(|| AppError::NotFound(format!("article '{slug}'")))?;
234	
235	    // Fetch tags.
236	    let tags: Vec<String> = {
237	        let rows: Vec<(String,)> = sqlx::query_as(
238	            "SELECT tag FROM content_tags WHERE content_id = $1 ORDER BY tag",
239	        )
240	        .bind(page.id)
241	        .fetch_all(pool.get_ref())
242	        .await
243	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
244	        rows.into_iter().map(|r| r.0).collect()
245	    };
246	
247	    // Fetch related: same category OR shared tags, ranked by category match.
248	    let related: Vec<ContentSummary> = sqlx::query_as(
249	        "SELECT DISTINCT cp.id, cp.slug, cp.title, cp.category, cp.route_id,
250	                cp.is_published, cp.quality_score, cp.publish_date, cp.updated_at
251	         FROM content_pages cp
252	         WHERE cp.is_published = TRUE
253	           AND cp.id <> $1
254	           AND (
255	               cp.category = $2
256	               OR EXISTS (
257	                   SELECT 1 FROM content_tags t1
258	                   JOIN content_tags t2 ON t1.tag = t2.tag
259	                   WHERE t1.content_id = $1 AND t2.content_id = cp.id
260	               )
261	           )
262	         ORDER BY
263	             CASE WHEN cp.category = $2 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
264	             cp.updated_at DESC
265	         LIMIT 5",
266	    )
267	    .bind(page.id)
268	    .bind(&page.category)
269	    .fetch_all(pool.get_ref())
270	    .await
271	    .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
272	
273	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ArticleResponse {
274	        article: ContentPageWithTags { page, tags },
275	        related,
276	    }))
277	}

1	//! Core policy engine.
2	//!
3	//! `RulesEngine` is constructed cheaply per-request and fetches each rule
4	//! value from the DB on demand.  Because the table is small and the read path
5	//! is already DB-bound, there is no in-memory cache — changes propagate
6	//! instantly without a restart.
7	//!
8	//! # Refund tier logic
9	//!
10	//! ```text
11	//!   hours_until_departure > refund_full_hours (24)
12	//!       → FullMinusFee   — fare − processing_fee ($5.00)
13	//!
14	//!   refund_partial_hours (2) < hours ≤ refund_full_hours (24)
15	//!       → HalfFare       — fare × 50 %
16	//!
17	//!   hours ≤ refund_partial_hours (2) AND disruption_flag = true
18	//!       → ServiceDisruption — full fare
19	//!
20	//!   hours ≤ refund_partial_hours (2) AND disruption_flag = false
21	//!       → RefundBlocked  (AppError::RefundBlocked)
22	//! ```

68	    /// Compute the wall-clock expiry for a new held order.
69	    pub async fn hold_expiry(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> {
70	        Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::minutes(self.hold_ttl_minutes().await)
71	    }
72	
73	    // ── Refund policy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	
75	    /// Evaluate refund eligibility for a cancelled order.
76	    ///
77	    /// All four possible outcomes map to distinct DB rule keys so that ops
78	    /// can tune each threshold independently without redeploying.
79	    ///
80	    /// Returns `Err(AppError::RefundBlocked)` when the order is past the
81	    /// late window and no service disruption is flagged.
82	    pub async fn evaluate_refund(
83	        &self,
84	        departure_time:  DateTime<Utc>,
85	        fare_amount:     Decimal,
86	        disruption_flag: bool,
87	    ) -> AppResult<RefundDecision> {
88	        let full_hours    = self.load_i64("refund_full_hours",    rules::FULL_REFUND_HOURS).await;
89	        let partial_hours = self.load_i64("refund_partial_hours", rules::PARTIAL_REFUND_HOURS).await;
90	
91	        let fee_str = self.repo
92	            .get_value("refund_processing_fee_usd", rules::REFUND_PROCESSING_FEE_USD)
93	            .await;
94	        let processing_fee: Decimal = fee_str
95	            .parse()
96	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| rules::REFUND_PROCESSING_FEE_USD.parse().expect("valid constant"));
97	
98	        // Signed — negative means the departure is already past.
99	        let hours_until = (departure_time - Utc::now()).num_hours();
100	
101	        let (outcome, max_amount, reason) = if hours_until > full_hours {
102	            let amt = (fare_amount - processing_fee).max(Decimal::ZERO);
103	            (
104	                RefundOutcome::FullMinusFee,
105	                amt,
106	                format!(
107	                    "Departure in {}h (>{} h window) — full refund minus ${} processing fee",
108	                    hours_until, full_hours, processing_fee,
109	                ),
110	            )
111	        } else if hours_until > partial_hours {
112	            let half = Decimal::new(5, 1); // 0.5
113	            let amt  = (fare_amount * half).round_dp(2);
114	            (
115	                RefundOutcome::HalfFare,
116	                amt,
117	                format!(
118	                    "Departure in {}h ({}-{} h window) — 50% partial refund",
119	                    hours_until, partial_hours, full_hours,
120	                ),
121	            )
122	        } else if disruption_flag {
123	            (
124	                RefundOutcome::ServiceDisruption,
125	                fare_amount,
126	                format!(
127	                    "Service disruption exception — full fare refund despite {}h window",
128	                    hours_until,
129	                ),
130	            )
131	        } else {
132	            return Err(AppError::RefundBlocked(format!(
133	                "Departure in {}h — refund window is closed (<{} h). \
134	                 Flag a service disruption first if an incident applies.",
135	                hours_until, partial_hours,
136	            )));
137	        };
138	
139	        Ok(RefundDecision { outcome, max_amount, reason })
140	    }
141	
142	    // ── Internal helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
143	
144	    async fn load_i64(&self, key: &str, default: i64) -> i64 {
145	        self.repo
146	            .get_value(key, &default.to_string())
147	            .await
148	            .parse::<i64>()
149	            .unwrap_or(default)
150	    }
151	}

47	        params: &ListCredentialsParams,
48	    ) -> AppResult<PaginatedResponse<Credential>> {
49	        let per_page = params.pagination.per_page();
50	        let offset   = params.pagination.offset();
51	        let page     = params.pagination.page();
52	
53	        let total: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
54	            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credentials
55	             WHERE ($1::UUID IS NULL OR contractor_id = $1)
56	               AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR status        = $2)",
57	        )
58	        .bind(params.contractor_id)
59	        .bind(&params.status)
60	        .fetch_one(self.0)
61	        .await
62	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
63	
64	        let items: Vec<Credential> = sqlx::query_as(
65	            "SELECT id, contractor_id, document_type, file_name, file_path,
66	                    file_size_bytes, mime_type, fingerprint, expires_at, status,
67	                    uploaded_by, uploaded_at, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, review_notes
68	             FROM credentials
69	             WHERE ($1::UUID IS NULL OR contractor_id = $1)
70	               AND ($2::TEXT IS NULL OR status        = $2)
71	             ORDER BY uploaded_at DESC
72	             LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4",
73	        )
74	        .bind(params.contractor_id)
75	        .bind(&params.status)
76	        .bind(per_page)
77	        .bind(offset)
78	        .fetch_all(self.0)
79	        .await
80	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
81	
82	        let total_pages = (total + per_page - 1) / per_page;
83	        Ok(PaginatedResponse { items, total, page, per_page, total_pages })
84	    }

1	//! Centralised error type for the RailOps backend.
2	//!
3	//! Every handler returns `AppResult<T>` which is `Result<T, AppError>`.
4	//! `AppError` implements `actix_web::ResponseError` so Actix converts it to
5	//! a structured JSON response automatically.
6	
7	use actix_web::{http::StatusCode, HttpResponse, ResponseError};
8	use serde_json::json;
9	use thiserror::Error;
10	use tracing::error;
11	
12	pub type AppResult<T> = Result<T, AppError>;
13	
14	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
15	pub enum AppError {
16	    // ── Auth / access ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	    #[error("Authentication required: {0}")]
18	    Unauthorized(String),
19	
20	    #[error("Permission denied: {0}")]
21	    Forbidden(String),
22	
23	    #[error("Account locked until {0}")]
24	    AccountLocked(String),
25	
26	    // ── Input / validation ────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	    #[error("Validation error: {0}")]
28	    Validation(String),
29	
30	    #[error("Not found: {0}")]
31	    NotFound(String),
32	
33	    #[error("Conflict: {0}")]
34	    Conflict(String),
35	
36	    // ── Business rules ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
37	    #[error("Refund blocked: {0}")]
38	    RefundBlocked(String),
39	
40	    #[error("Order hold expired")]
41	    HoldExpired,
42	
43	    #[error("Quality score too low to publish ({0}/100)")]
44	    QualityBelowThreshold(String),
45	
46	    // ── Rate limiting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
47	    #[error("Rate limit exceeded — try again in {retry_after}s")]
48	    RateLimited { retry_after: u64 },
49	
50	    // ── File / upload ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	    #[error("Unsupported file type: {0}")]
52	    UnsupportedFileType(String),
53	
54	    #[error("File too large (max 10 MB)")]
55	    FileTooLarge,
56	
57	    // ── Infrastructure ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
58	    #[error("Database error")]
59	    Database(#[from] sqlx::Error),
60	
61	    #[error("IO error")]
62	    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
63	
64	    #[error("Serialization error")]
65	    Serialization(#[from] serde_json::Error),
66	
67	    /// Catch-all for unexpected failures — avoids leaking internals.
68	    #[error("Internal server error")]
69	    Internal(#[from] anyhow::Error),
70	}
71	
72	impl AppError {
73	    fn status_code_inner(&self) -> StatusCode {
74	        match self {
75	            AppError::Unauthorized(_)         => StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
76	            AppError::Forbidden(_)            => StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
77	            AppError::AccountLocked(_)        => StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
78	            AppError::Validation(_)           => StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
79	            AppError::NotFound(_)             => StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
80	            AppError::Conflict(_)             => StatusCode::CONFLICT,
81	            AppError::RefundBlocked(_)        => StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
82	            AppError::HoldExpired             => StatusCode::GONE,
83	            AppError::QualityBelowThreshold(_)=> StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
84	            AppError::RateLimited { .. }      => StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
85	            AppError::UnsupportedFileType(_)  => StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
86	            AppError::FileTooLarge            => StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,
87	            AppError::Database(_)
88	            | AppError::Io(_)
89	            | AppError::Serialization(_)
90	            | AppError::Internal(_)           => StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
91	        }
92	    }
93	
94	    fn error_type(&self) -> &'static str {
95	        match self {
96	            AppError::Unauthorized(_)          => "unauthorized",
97	            AppError::Forbidden(_)             => "forbidden",
98	            AppError::AccountLocked(_)         => "account_locked",
99	            AppError::Validation(_)            => "validation_error",
100	            AppError::NotFound(_)              => "not_found",
101	            AppError::Conflict(_)              => "conflict",
102	            AppError::RefundBlocked(_)         => "refund_blocked",
103	            AppError::HoldExpired              => "hold_expired",
104	            AppError::QualityBelowThreshold(_) => "quality_below_threshold",
105	            AppError::RateLimited { .. }       => "rate_limited",
106	            AppError::UnsupportedFileType(_)   => "unsupported_file_type",
107	            AppError::FileTooLarge             => "file_too_large",
108	            AppError::Database(_)              => "database_error",
109	            AppError::Io(_)                    => "io_error",
110	            AppError::Serialization(_)         => "serialization_error",
111	            AppError::Internal(_)              => "internal_error",
112	        }
113	    }
114	}
115	
116	impl ResponseError for AppError {
117	    fn status_code(&self) -> StatusCode {
118	        self.status_code_inner()
119	    }
120	
121	    fn error_response(&self) -> HttpResponse {
122	        let status = self.status_code_inner();
123	
124	        // Log internal errors with full detail; never expose them to clients.
125	        if status == StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR {
126	            error!(error = %self, "Internal server error");
127	        }
128	
129	        // The client-facing message strips internal detail for 5xx.
130	        let client_message = match status.is_server_error() {
131	            true  => "An internal error occurred. Please contact support.",
132	            false => &self.to_string(),
133	        };
134	
135	        let mut body = json!({
136	            "error": {
137	                "type":    self.error_type(),
138	                "code":    status.as_u16(),
139	                "message": client_message,
140	            }
141	        });
142	
143	        // Add Retry-After hint for rate-limited responses.
144	        if let AppError::RateLimited { retry_after } = self {
145	            body["error"]["retry_after"] = json!(retry_after);
146	        }
147	
148	        HttpResponse::build(status).json(body)
149	    }
150	}

```rust
pub async fn list_subscriptions(

) -> AppResult<HttpResponse> {
```

```rust
    let dispatcher_subs = SubscriptionRepo::new(&pool)
        .list_for_subscriber("dispatcher", auth.id)
        .await?;
    let contractor_subs = SubscriptionRepo::new(&pool)
        .list_for_subscriber("contractor", auth.id)
```

14	ARG RUST_VERSION=1.88
15	
16	# ── Stage 1: base toolchain ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	FROM rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm AS chef
18	# Pure-Rust TLS (rustls) + RustCrypto mean we need no system OpenSSL headers.
19	# gcc and libc6-dev are already present in rust:slim-bookworm and are
20	# sufficient for ring's bundled C/asm compilation.
21	
22	RUN cargo install cargo-chef --locked
23	WORKDIR /src
24	
25	# ── Stage 2: dependency planner ───────────────────────────────────────────────
26	FROM chef AS planner
27	COPY . .
28	RUN cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json
29	
30	# ── Stage 3: backend build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	FROM chef AS backend-builder
32	
33	COPY --from=planner /src/recipe.json recipe.json
34	# Pre-compile all backend dependencies (layer is reused on code-only changes).
35	RUN cargo chef cook --release -p backend --recipe-path recipe.json
36	
37	COPY . .
38	RUN cargo build --release -p backend
39	
40	# ── Stage 4: frontend (WASM) build ────────────────────────────────────────────
41	FROM chef AS frontend-builder
42	
43	# WASM compilation target
44	RUN rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
45	
46	# trunk: Yew asset bundler (downloads wasm-bindgen-cli automatically)
47	RUN cargo install trunk --locked
48	
49	# Install curl + CA certificates to download the Tailwind standalone binary.
50	# This is a build-time-only dependency; the runtime image has no internet access.
51	RUN apt-get update -qq \
52	    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates \
53	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
54	
55	# ── Tailwind CSS standalone CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────
56	# Single self-contained binary — no Node.js required.
57	# Scans ./src/**/*.rs and ./index.html for used utility classes, then generates
58	# a minified CSS bundle (tailwind.css) that trunk copies into the dist folder.
59	ARG TAILWIND_VERSION=3.4.1
60	RUN set -eux; \
61	    ARCH=$(uname -m); \
62	    case "$ARCH" in \
63	        x86_64)  TW_ARCH=x64   ;; \
64	        aarch64) TW_ARCH=arm64 ;; \
65	        *) echo "Unsupported CPU architecture: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
66	    esac; \
67	    curl -fsSLo /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss \
68	        "https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/releases/download/v${TAILWIND_VERSION}/tailwindcss-linux-${TW_ARCH}" \
69	    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss \
70	    && test -x /usr/local/bin/tailwindcss
71	
72	# ── Dependency pre-warm (frontend + shared) ───────────────────────────────────
73	COPY --from=planner /src/recipe.json recipe.json
74	RUN cargo chef cook --release -p frontend --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
75	    --recipe-path recipe.json
76	
77	# ── Full source copy and build ────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	COPY . .
79	WORKDIR /src/frontend
80	
81	# 1. Generate the Tailwind CSS bundle from Rust source files + config.
82	#    Output: frontend/tailwind.css (picked up by trunk via <link data-trunk>)
83	RUN tailwindcss \
84	    --input  ./src/app.css \
85	    --output ./tailwind.css \
86	    --config ./tailwind.config.js \
87	    --minify
88	
89	# 2. Compile Yew to WASM and assemble the static dist/ folder.
90	RUN trunk build --release
91	
92	# ── Stage 5: test runner ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
93	# Inherits the full Rust toolchain + all pre-compiled dependencies.
94	# Used exclusively by `docker compose --profile test run --rm tester`.
95	FROM backend-builder AS tester
96	
97	# curl is needed for the in-container health-check wait loop.
98	RUN apt-get update -qq \
99	    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
100	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
101	
102	WORKDIR /src
103	
104	# Default command: full test suite (overridden by docker-compose).
105	CMD ["sh", "-c", \
106	    "cargo test --bin backend -p backend -- --nocapture && \
107	     cargo test -p shared -- --nocapture && \
108	     cargo test --test api_integration_test -p backend -- --nocapture"]
109	
110	# ── Stage 6: minimal runtime image ────────────────────────────────────────────
111	FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS runtime
112	# curl is used by the Docker Compose healthcheck to probe /health over HTTPS.
113	# It is the only package needed at runtime; ca-certificates is not required
114	# because the app generates its own TLS cert (rcgen) and connects to Postgres
115	# only on the internal Docker network.
116	RUN apt-get update -qq \
117	    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
118	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
119	
120	RUN groupadd -r railops \
121	    && useradd -r -g railops -u 1001 railops
122	
123	WORKDIR /app
124	
125	# Backend binary
126	COPY --from=backend-builder  /src/target/release/backend   /app/railops
127	
128	# Compiled Yew WASM + HTML + bundled Tailwind CSS
129	COPY --from=frontend-builder /src/frontend/dist            /app/static
130	
131	RUN mkdir -p /app/uploads /app/certs \
132	    && chown -R railops:railops /app
133	
134	USER railops
135	EXPOSE 8443
136	
137	HEALTHCHECK NONE
138	CMD ["/app/railops"]
139

18

20	
21	| Username     | Password            | Role       |
